subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin concludes that at our level, you need to mean it, and by the time you're facing whatever's waiting on the surface, you'd better be doing something significant every time you swing.

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considers drinking a potion of giant strength when it matters rather than investing in permanent strength increases, recognizing this as a new bad habit.
source_quote: The logic: skip the investment, drink the potion of giant strength when it matters. Which — I recognized, even as I thought it — had given me one more bad habit to account for.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin describes the quiet knock inside the chest as the sign of crossing a threshold he didn't notice crossing, and acknowledges he's felt it before after bad fights.
source_quote: Something hit me, as I surveyed the battlefield. Not literally. Though, given how the last several months have gone, that's worth specifying. No, this was the other kind of thing — the quiet knock inside the chest that means you've crossed some threshold you didn't notice crossing. I've felt it before, in the dark, after bad fights.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin feels that he has crossed a threshold he didn't notice, becoming bigger and more present.
source_quote: Something hit me, as I surveyed the battlefield. Not literally. Though, given how the last several months have gone, that's worth specifying. No, this was the other kind of thing — the quiet knock inside the chest that means you've crossed some threshold you didn't notice crossing. I've felt it before, in the dark, after bad fights. The body takes stock before the mind does. I was bigger somehow. More there.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin found the Ember Grapple very funny.
source_quote: Thorin said something about "the Ember Grapple." Someone — possibly Thorin again, possibly Grygum, it is hard to tell when they are both making noise — found this very funny.

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin has acquired proficiency with thrown weapons, specifically javelins, and proposed the name 'Ember Grapple' for Zalthir and Daz’s new tactic, finding humor in the contrast between the team’s tactical pragmatism and heroic narratives, and suggesting practical gap-control solutions for upcoming engagements.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin has come to accept that survival in the Underdark requires doing what others won't, and he now understands the Zhentarim’s pragmatism better than he would have liked.
source_quote: The Zhentarim have survived by being willing to do what others won't. I understood that better now than I would have liked.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin identifies Zhentarim Tactics as a ruthless, effective, and uncomfortable school of thought that he is considering adopting, acknowledging his own dark transition from a happy-go-lucky kid to someone who understands the Underdark doesn't care who you want to be.
source_quote: There's a school of thought — brutal, efficient, not entirely reputable — that goes by the name Zhentarim Tactics. Ruthless by design. Effective in ways that decent people find uncomfortable. ... The happy-go-lucky kid who went underground expecting something survivable has spent months watching demon lords and eating mushrooms and coming to understand that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin

subject: Zalthir

subject: Zalthir

I think it was Brother Heslin — or possibly that was the one who taught falling. I'm genuinely uncertain. Either way, I remember the light through the shuttered window and thinking the form was taking too long. I did not remember what they said. I am currently learning it from a Drow wizard in a tunnel.

subject: Zalthir

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understands that grapple is a quick action, but binding with rope consumes the full action, making setup a two-turn process that locks down one enemy for maximum damage.
source_quote: Grapple is a quick thing — one motion, a grab, a test of weight and leverage, done in the space of a heartbeat. That leaves the hands. Rope is slower. Tying something takes focus, takes both hands, takes the better part of a turn spent crouching over a target that is probably trying to bite you. The grapple could happen in the spare moment before my main action. The binding would consume the action itself. The whole turn — both pieces of it — spent on one enemy, pinned to the floor, with Daz's daggers already spinning above them.

subject: Zalthir

The next turn, I would be free — and whatever I had tied down would still be there, still bleeding, while I moved to the next problem.

subject: Cloud of Daggers

subject: Ember Grapple identity

subject: free casting utility
fact: The strategic value of free castings — particularly Misty Step — is emerging as a core principle for Daz, who sees them as resources that cost nothing in the moment they matter most.
source_quote: A slot is a resource. A free casting is a resource that costs nothing in the moment you need it most, which is usually the moment you can least afford to spend anything.

subject: lack of long rest
fact: The group will not take a long rest before the next encounter, and all resources — spells, equipment, stamina — must be carried forward without replenishment, creating pressure to optimize every action and spell in the upcoming fight.

subject: lack of ranged capability
fact: The party has no ranged weapons or abilities, creating a critical vulnerability that will inevitably be exploited by flying or distant enemies as they approach the surface world.
source_quote: Which is also why not having anyone who can reach a flying enemy is going to come back and bite us.

subject: potion hoarding habit

source_quote: The potion you don't drink is the potion you die holding. Wrong strategy, but that's just how I roll.

subject: the long arrangement
fact: The concept of 'the long arrangement' — that preparation, positioning, and spell synergy constitute the true battle — is an evolving theory Daz is refining, blending Milo Goodbarrel’s terrain lessons with his own Evoker philosophy.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel had a chapter about this. He called it 'the long arrangement'... I always thought he was selling short the part about spell selection.

subject: Thorin's potential shift to Zhentarim Tactics

source_quote: That would be a whole change of character for you. Well, I mean, I can work it into my story. I could. It would be honest, even. Not the honesty I prefer — I've always liked honesty you can stand behind without flinching — but there are things you absorb down here whether you mean to or not.

subject: uncertain monastery lesson
fact: Zalthir remembers the light through a shuttered window and the feeling that a monastery lesson on battlefield geometry took too long, but cannot recall what was said or who taught it — leaving the origin of the 'Ember Grapple' concept partially mythic, possibly inherited from a forgotten teacher.
